issue_payload.body:
Based on fneitzel prototype ([Added prototype of InputTextArea](https://github.com/BabylonJS/Babylon.js/pull/8275)), I improved the component to support the margin, the deletion (backspace/del.), the highlighting, deadkeys and copy/paste/cut shortcuts.

A lot of things remained to do :
- fix the CR on last line
- find why the text clip on single line during autostreching
- resolve todos
- clean/fix/update the code

My approach was highly naïve, so maybe a cleaner architecture will be necessery.

discussion_timeline.author: fneitzel
discussion_timeline.body: Cool that you are finishing it, let me know if you need help.

discussion_timeline.author: RaananW
discussion_timeline.body: I also wait for @DarraghBurkeMS's review to test the actual functionality.

discussion_timeline.author: Popov72
discussion_timeline.body:
> Why not use a textarea as the backend of this component and allow the browser to do the heavy-lifting of text editing?

What about Native if using a textarea HTML element under the hood?

discussion_timeline.author: RaananW
discussion_timeline.body:
> What about Native if using a textarea HTML element under the hood?

That's a good point. @bghgary , is there some corresponding element to be used, or does the functionality needs to be (re) implemented?

discussion_timeline.author: darraghjburke
discussion_timeline.body:
I'm not Gary, but: I don't think we can depend on any external text area implementation in Babylon Native. One of the critical design choices is that it's "bring your own UI", so we can't rely on any particular one of the many cross-platform UI solutions out there. The goal AFAIK is to implement enough of the canvas API that we can support Babylon GUI, but Babylon Native has no plans to support any DOM features (at that point we'd be making a browser.)

From my POV, having a Babylon GUI text area brings a lot of value, but it's also worth keeping in mind that it will probably be significantly harder to maintain than our existing controls. That being said, I love that you've taken a stab at it, and I'll definitely give it a try later this week :)

discussion_timeline.author: deltakosh
discussion_timeline.body: Totally aligned with @darraghjburke : no external dependencies beside just canvas API

discussion_timeline.author: bghgary
discussion_timeline.body:
> What about Native if using a textarea HTML element under the hood?

Maybe @CedricGuillemet can answer this part.

In general, I'm also curious if there are any localization concerns with this change.

discussion_timeline.author: Valerian-Perez-Wanadev
discussion_timeline.body: Thanks a lot for all your feedbacks, I'll fix that later in the week!

discussion_timeline.author: CedricGuillemet
discussion_timeline.body:
> > What about Native if using a textarea HTML element under the hood?
> 
> Maybe @CedricGuillemet can answer this part.
> 

Hard to tell without testing. At the current state, (basic) text and shape rendering will work. Idk if any unimplemented method is needed here.

discussion_timeline.author: deltakosh
discussion_timeline.body:
@Valerian-Perez-Wanadev : @fneitzel is interested to contribute to your PR. Do you mind opening your branch for his PR?

Anyway I recommend the 2 of you to chat as your code is based on @fneitzel one

discussion_timeline.author: Valerian-Perez-Wanadev
discussion_timeline.body:
I've made some good improvments during the sart of the year but I'm in a dilemma...

The component inherits from InputText, but it acts like a TextBlock. So for the textWrapping behaviour, I must follow the implementation of only Clip/WordWrap or Clip/WordWrap/Ellipsis/WordWrapEllipsis?

Furthermore, the ellipsis mode it's not very useful in InputTextArea... I choose to discard it for the moment. But I want to known your thoughts about this before merging my code.

discussion_timeline.author: deltakosh
discussion_timeline.body: For things in common we can think about having a common ancestor?

discussion_timeline.author: Valerian-Perez-Wanadev
discussion_timeline.body:
> For things in common we can think about having a common ancestor?

Of course I will do thatif needed but actually my choice is on which behaviour to adopt. 

After seeing implementation of TextArea of Firefox and the InputText of BJS, I will keep their philosophy and let the user decides whether their add a line or let the component breaks the text alone. It's more natural to do it that way.

discussion_timeline.author: deltakosh
discussion_timeline.body:
> It's more natural to do it that way.

Agreed

discussion_timeline.author: Valerian-Perez-Wanadev
discussion_timeline.body:
I have a question about the Enter key.

How can I override the blur by hitting Enter ? 

I want to add a new line with Enter but I can't figure how to do without blurring the input...

discussion_timeline.author: deltakosh
discussion_timeline.body: the onkeydown can be cancelled if you detect Enter (preventDefault)

issue_payload.body:
This commit adds support of native base64 encoding/decoding api support, which is benchmarked to be faster then the js impl. It checks native support of the native api excluding polyfills by core-js and es-shims on module load, and fallback to the original js impl for backward compatibility.
See this forum post for discussion and benchmark result: <https://forum.babylonjs.com/t/es2026-proposal-arraybuffer-base64-support/62715>

commit_history.message:
stringTools: ES2026 proposal-arraybuffer-base64 support

This commit adds support of native base64 encoding/decoding api support, which is benchmarked to be faster then the js impl.
It checks native support of the native api excluding polyfills by core-js and es-shims on module load, and fallback to the original js impl for backward compatibility.
See this forum post for discussion and benchmark result: <https://forum.babylonjs.com/t/es2026-proposal-arraybuffer-base64-support/62715>

issue_payload.body:
I want to be able to load a custom NRG in the viewer. To do this, I've made some changes to `viewer.ts`:
 * A new protected method, `_setActiveFrameGraph` gives derived classes a way to activate a custom FrameGraph and keep its mesh lists in sync with the scene as models load and unload.

I also made some changes to `TransmissionHelper.ts` to support unbinding things when needed. In my test viewer, I was loading a frame graph after already potentially loading a scene with transmission and needed these fixes.
